key_insight: Routing codes are a new qLDPC family that keeps high encoding rates while making non-local couplings shorter, fewer, and fully parallel.
engineering_relevance: By eliminating wiring crossings in superconducting layouts and simplifying atom movement in neutral-atom systems, routing codes are designed for easier hardware implementation than prior high-rate qLDPC proposals.
method: Constructed a qLDPC family with explicit high-rate code instances.
Reduced qubit connectivity and shortened non-local coupling lengths.
Made all non-local couplings mutually parallel to simplify hardware routing and scheduling.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations show weight-7 routing codes can cut physical qubit overhead by about 8× versus surface codes at the same logical error rate.
watch_item: The results are promising for hardware feasibility, but real devices still need to confirm performance under fabrication constraints, crosstalk, and control errors.
paper_title: Routing Codes: High-Rate Quantum LDPC Codes with Short, Parallel Non-Local Connectivity
